problem: Wire a push-button-controlled LED indicator on a +5V rail with a current-limit resistor, producing a KiCad schematic that passes ERC with zero violations.
assumptions: +5V rail already regulated and available
SMD 0805 passives; PTS645 SMD tact switch
KiCad standard libraries: Switch:SW_Push, Device:R, Device:LED, power:+5V, power:GND
steps: Add SW1 = Switch:SW_Push (Button_Switch_SMD:SW_SPST_PTS645Sx43SMTR92), R1 = Device:R 330R (R_0805), D1 = Device:LED (LED_0805), plus power symbols #PWR01 power:+5V and #PWR02 power:GND.
Net '+5V': SW1 pin 1 + #PWR01 pin 1.
Net 'SW_R': SW1 pin 2 -> R1 pin 1.
Net 'R_LED': R1 pin 2 -> D1 pin 2 (D1 pin 2 is the ANODE in Device:LED).
Net 'GND': D1 pin 1 (cathode) + #PWR02 pin 1.

Layout (checked-in golden file): signal flow left-to-right on one row, supplies at the ends; R1 rotated 90 degrees so pin 1 lands on the left (probe-verified); PWR_FLAG symbols (#FLG01/#FLG02) placed next to the power symbols.
result: Series chain topology: +5V -- SW1 -- R1(330R) -- LED(anode->cathode) -- GND. Four nets, three components, two power symbols. Passed kicad-cli ERC 0, connectivity round-trip, and SVG render.
failure_modes: LED polarity swap: in Device:LED, pin 1 = cathode (K), pin 2 = anode (A). Connecting pin 1 to the resistor reverses the diode.
Missing PWR_FLAG on power nets fed only by passive parts triggers KiCad 'power pin not driven' ERC errors.
design_notes: 330R at 5V gives roughly 9-10 mA through a typical LED (Vf ~2V) — safe generic indicator value.
Symbol rotation matters for readable layout: Device:R at rot 90 puts pin 1 on the left; this was probe-verified, not assumed.
statement: Wire a push-button-controlled LED indicator on a +5V rail with a current-limit resistor, producing a KiCad schematic that passes ERC with zero violations.

problem: Minimal bring-up circuit for an STM32G474RETx (LQFP-64): full power/decoupling, reset, boot strap, and a 10-pin ARM SWD debug connector, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.
assumptions: Single regulated +3V3 rail powers everything (VBAT tied to VDD; no battery backup)
Boot from main flash (BOOT0 strapped low)
Debug via SWD only (no JTAG, no SWO trace)
Libraries: MCU_ST_STM32G4:STM32G474RETx, Connector:Conn_ARM_JTAG_SWD_10
steps: Add U1 STM32G474RETx (LQFP-64), J1 Conn_ARM_JTAG_SWD_10 (2x05 1.27mm header), C1-C4 0.1uF (one per VDD pin), C5 0.1uF (VDDA), C6 10uF bulk, C7 0.1uF (NRST), R1 10k (BOOT0 pull-down), power symbols +3V3 and GND.
Net '+3V3': U1 pins 1 (VBAT), 16/32/48/64 (VDD), 29 (VDDA), 28 (VREF+); C1-C6 pin 1; J1 pin 1 (VTref); #PWR01.
Net 'GND': U1 pins 15, 27 (VSSA), and the HIDDEN STACKED VSS pins 31/47/63; C1-C7 pin 2; R1 pin 2; J1 pins 3 (GND), 5 (hidden stacked GND), 9 (GNDDetect); #PWR02.
Net 'NRST': U1 pin 7 (PG10/NRST) + C7 pin 1 (100nF to GND) + J1 pin 10 (nRESET).
Net 'BOOT0': U1 pin 61 (PB8-BOOT0) + R1 pin 1 (10k to GND).
Net 'SWDIO': U1 pin 49 (PA13) + J1 pin 2. Net 'SWCLK': U1 pin 50 (PA14) + J1 pin 4.
Mark every remaining MCU pin (all of 1-64 not in the used set) as an explicit no-connect; also NC J1 pin 6 (SWO) and pin 8 (TDI). J1 pin 7 (KEY) is NC-typed in the library and needs no marker.
result: Star power topology: one +3V3 net fanning to 7 MCU supply pins + 6 caps + SWD VTref; one GND net absorbing 5 VSS pins (2 visible + 3 hidden stacked), all cap returns, BOOT0 pull-down return, and 3 SWD connector grounds. Four signal nets: NRST (with 100nF), BOOT0 (10k down), SWDIO, SWCLK. 48 explicit NC pins on U1 + 2 on J1. Passed kicad-cli ERC 0.
failure_modes: Hidden stacked VSS pins: STM32G474RETx LQFP-64 has VSS pins 31, 47, 63 stacked/hidden under pin 15 in the KiCad symbol. Missing them from the GND net leaves unconnected power-input pins -> ERC errors and a wrong netlist.
NRST is shared with PG10 (pin 7) on STM32G4 — there is no dedicated reset-only pin; if PG10 is repurposed as GPIO the reset circuit breaks.
BOOT0 is shared with PB8 (pin 61) on STM32G4 — it is NOT a dedicated boot pin as on older STM32 families; leaving it floating causes random boot-mode selection.

Conn_ARM_JTAG_SWD_10 has a hidden stacked GND pin (pin 5) and a GNDDetect pin (pin 9) that must both be tied to GND, plus a KEY pin (7) that is already NC-typed — adding an NC marker to a NC-typed pin is redundant, omitting GND on pin 5 is an ERC error.
Any unused MCU pin without an explicit no-connect marker produces an ERC 'unconnected pin' violation — ERC 0 requires exhaustive NC marking.
design_notes: Decoupling recipe verified: one 100nF per VDD pin (4x), a dedicated 100nF on VDDA, one 10uF bulk, plus 100nF on NRST for reset immunity.
VREF+ (pin 28) tied directly to +3V3 (no external reference).
VBAT (pin 1) tied to +3V3 when no backup battery is used.
SWD needs only 4 wires to the target: VTref, GND, SWDIO (PA13), SWCLK (PA14); nRESET on J1 pin 10 is optional-but-wired here.
statement: Minimal bring-up circuit for an STM32G474RETx (LQFP-64): full power/decoupling, reset, boot strap, and a 10-pin ARM SWD debug connector, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.

problem: Attach an Si7050-A20 I2C temperature sensor to an STM32G474RETx over I2C1 with proper pull-ups, plus the full minimal MCU hookup, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.
assumptions: Single +3V3 rail; standard-mode I2C (10k pull-ups acceptable)
I2C1 mapped to PB9 (SDA, AF4) and PA15 (SCL, AF4)
BOOT0 strapped low; no SWD connector in this fixture
Libraries: Sensor_Temperature:Si7050-A20 (DFN-6)
steps: Add U1 STM32G474RETx, U2 Si7050-A20, C1-C5 0.1uF (four VDD pins + VDDA), C6 10uF bulk, C7 0.1uF sensor decoupling, R1/R2 10k (SDA/SCL pull-ups), R3 10k (BOOT0 pull-down), +3V3 and GND power symbols.
Net '+3V3': U1 pins 1/16/28/29/32/48/64 (VBAT, 4x VDD, VREF+, VDDA); U2 pin 5 (sensor VDD); C1-C7 pin 1; R1 pin 1, R2 pin 1; #PWR01.
Net 'GND': U1 pins 15/27/31/47/63 (incl. hidden stacked VSS 31/47/63); U2 pin 2; C1-C7 pin 2; R3 pin 2; #PWR02.
Net 'SDA': U1 pin 62 (PB9 = I2C1_SDA) + U2 pin 1 + R1 pin 2.
Net 'SCL': U1 pin 51 (PA15 = I2C1_SCL) + U2 pin 6 + R2 pin 2.
Net 'BOOT0': U1 pin 61 (PB8/BOOT0) + R3 pin 1 (strap low via 10k).
Explicit no-connect on every unused U1 pin. Sensor pins 3/4 are NC-typed in the library and need no marker.
result: Bus topology: shared SDA and SCL nets each carry MCU pin + sensor pin + one 10k pull-up to +3V3. Sensor has its own local 100nF. Nets named exactly 'SDA'/'SCL' so the project i2c_pullup lint recognizes and checks them (removing R1/R2 provably triggers the i2c_pullup_missing lint in tests). Passed kicad-cli ERC 0.
failure_modes: Missing I2C pull-ups: open-drain SDA/SCL with no pull-up never idles high — the bus is dead. The repo lint 'i2c_pullup_missing' fires when either resistor is absent.
Hidden stacked VSS pins 31/47/63 must be on GND (same trap as golden 2).

BOOT0 = PB8 (pin 61): note PB9 (pin 62) is used for SDA — the boot strap and the I2C pin are physically adjacent pins on the same port; confusing pin 61 with 62 both breaks boot and shorts the strap onto the bus.
Si7050 pins 3/4 are NC-typed in the KiCad library; adding NC markers to them is unnecessary (and pin-type-aware tools may flag it).
design_notes: Pin-to-signal mapping is package-specific and was verified against the real part index: PB9 = pin 62 = I2C1_SDA (AF4), PA15 = pin 51 = I2C1_SCL (AF4) on LQFP-64.
10k pull-ups are fine for standard-mode/low-capacitance short traces; use 2.2k-4.7k for fast mode or longer buses.
Naming I2C nets exactly SDA/SCL (or with those substrings) makes them lintable — a convention worth keeping in generated designs.
statement: Attach an Si7050-A20 I2C temperature sensor to an STM32G474RETx over I2C1 with proper pull-ups, plus the full minimal MCU hookup, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.

problem: Attach a W25Q32JVSS SPI NOR flash (SOIC-8) to an STM32G474RETx over SPI1, handling /CS, /WP and /HOLD correctly, plus full minimal MCU hookup, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.
assumptions: Single +3V3 rail; standard 4-wire SPI (no quad mode — IO2//WP and IO3//HOLD used as control pins, not data)
SPI1 on PA5/PA6/PA7 with software chip-select on PA4
Libraries: Memory_Flash:W25Q32JVSS (SOIC-8)
steps: Add U1 STM32G474RETx, U2 W25Q32JVSS, C1-C5 0.1uF (4x VDD + VDDA), C6 10uF bulk, C7 0.1uF flash VCC decoupling, R1 10k (/CS pull-up), R2 10k (/WP tie-high), R3 10k (/HOLD tie-high), +3V3 and GND symbols.
Net 'GND': U1 pins 15/27/31/47/63 (incl. hidden stacked VSS); U2 pin 4 (GND); C1-C7 pin 2; #PWR02.
Net 'SPI_SCK': U1 pin 19 (PA5) -> U2 pin 6 (CLK).
Net 'SPI_MISO': U1 pin 20 (PA6) <- U2 pin 2 (DO/IO1).
Net 'SPI_MOSI': U1 pin 21 (PA7) -> U2 pin 5 (DI/IO0).
Net 'SPI_CS': U1 pin 18 (PA4) + U2 pin 1 (/CS) + R1 pin 2 (10k pull-up to +3V3 so flash is deselected during MCU reset/boot).
Net 'FLASH_WP': U2 pin 3 (/WP) + R2 pin 2 (10k to +3V3). Net 'FLASH_HOLD': U2 pin 7 (/HOLD) + R3 pin 2 (10k to +3V3).
Explicit no-connect on every unused U1 pin.
result: Point-to-point SPI topology: three unidirectional data/clock nets MCU<->flash, a chip-select net with reset-safe pull-up, and two active-low control pins (/WP, /HOLD) each tied high through their own 10k. Flash gets local 100nF. Passed kicad-cli ERC 0.
failure_modes: /WP (pin 3) or /HOLD (pin 7) left floating or low: floating /HOLD can randomly pause the flash mid-transfer; low /WP write-protects status registers. Both must be tied high (10k) when quad mode is unused — the classic 'flash reads once then dies' bug.
/CS without a pull-up floats during MCU reset/bootloader, letting the flash see garbage clock edges as commands; the 10k pull-up on SPI_CS deselects it until firmware takes over.
MISO/MOSI naming trap on Winbond parts: DO = master-in (goes to MISO/PA6), DI = master-out (goes to MOSI/PA7). Crossing these is silent — ERC cannot catch it.
Hidden stacked VSS pins 31/47/63 must be on GND (same trap as golden 2).
design_notes: Pin map verified against the real part index: PA4=18, PA5=19 (SCK), PA6=20 (MISO), PA7=21 (MOSI) on LQFP-64.
Separate resistors per control pin (not a shared net) keep /WP and /HOLD independently reconfigurable to GPIOs later for quad-SPI.
Tie-highs go through 10k rather than direct to +3V3 so firmware can later drive the pins in quad mode without a rework.
statement: Attach a W25Q32JVSS SPI NOR flash (SOIC-8) to an STM32G474RETx over SPI1, handling /CS, /WP and /HOLD correctly, plus full minimal MCU hookup, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.

problem: STM32G474RETx with a 4-pin UART debug header, a 2-pin screw-terminal power input, and a GPIO-driven status LED, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.
assumptions: Regulated +3V3 arrives externally on the screw terminal (no on-board regulator)
USART1 on PA9 (TX) / PA10 (RX); 3.3V logic on the header (no RS-232 levels)
Header pinout convention: TX, RX, 3V3, GND
steps: Add U1 STM32G474RETx; J1 Connector:Screw_Terminal_01x02 (Phoenix MKDS 5.00mm) as PWR_IN; J2 Connector:Conn_01x04_Pin (2.54mm header) as UART; C1-C5 0.1uF (4x VDD + VDDA), C6 10uF bulk; R1 330R + D1 Device:LED for the status LED; +3V3 and GND symbols.
Net '+3V3': U1 pins 1/16/28/29/32/48/64; C1-C6 pin 1; J1 pin 1 (power in); J2 pin 3 (header 3V3); #PWR01.
Net 'GND': U1 pins 15/27/31/47/63 (incl. hidden stacked VSS); C1-C6 pin 2; J1 pin 2; J2 pin 4; D1 pin 1 (cathode); #PWR02.
Net 'UART_TX': U1 pin 43 (PA9 = USART1_TX) -> J2 pin 1.
Net 'UART_RX': U1 pin 44 (PA10 = USART1_RX) <- J2 pin 2.
Net 'LED_CTRL': U1 pin 19 (PA5, GPIO) -> R1 pin 1. Net 'LED_A': R1 pin 2 -> D1 pin 2 (anode). Cathode already on GND.
Explicit no-connect on every unused U1 pin.
result: Topology: external +3V3 enters on J1 and fans to MCU supplies, decoupling, and the UART header's power pin; UART is two point-to-point nets MCU->header; LED is the series chain GPIO(PA5) -> 330R -> LED anode -> cathode -> GND (GPIO sources current, active-high). Passed kicad-cli ERC 0.
failure_modes: Header TX/RX semantics: J2 pin 1 carries the MCU's TX — the attached USB-serial adapter must connect its RX there (null-modem crossing happens in the cable, not on the board). Labeling the header from the adapter's perspective double-crosses the pair.
LED polarity: Device:LED pin 1 = cathode, pin 2 = anode; the resistor must meet the anode (pin 2) in this active-high arrangement.
Hidden stacked VSS pins 31/47/63 must be on GND (same trap as golden 2).
Power-input nets fed only from a connector need PWR_FLAG in KiCad or ERC reports 'power input not driven'.
design_notes: Pin map verified: PA9 = pin 43 (USART1_TX), PA10 = pin 44 (USART1_RX), PA5 = pin 19 (GPIO for LED) on LQFP-64.
330R at 3.3V gives ~4 mA LED current (Vf ~2V) — well inside an STM32 GPIO's drive capability.
Providing 3V3 on the UART header powers low-current adapters/targets and gives probes a logic-level reference.
statement: STM32G474RETx with a 4-pin UART debug header, a 2-pin screw-terminal power input, and a GPIO-driven status LED, passing kicad-cli ERC with zero violations.

name: STM32 minimal power + reset + boot + SWD
problem: Any STM32 design needs a canonical support skeleton before peripherals: all supply pins powered and decoupled, reset conditioned, boot mode strapped, and a debug port attached.
assumptions: Single 3.3V rail; boot from main flash; SWD debug
steps: Power: connect ALL VDD pins + VBAT + VDDA + VREF+ to +3V3. Enumerate supply pins from the symbol/datasheet — KiCad MCU symbols hide stacked duplicate VSS/VDD pins (e.g. STM32G474RETx VSS at 31/47/63 stacked under 15); every one must be on the net.
Decoupling: one 100nF per physical VDD pin, one dedicated 100nF at VDDA, one bulk 10uF on the rail.
Reset: NRST to a 100nF cap to GND, and route NRST to the debug connector's nRESET pin. Internal pull-up exists; no external pull-up needed.
Boot strap: BOOT0 through 10k to GND for flash boot (10k to +3V3 for system bootloader). Never float it.

SWD: Conn_ARM_JTAG_SWD_10 — pin 1 VTref to +3V3, pins 3/5/9 to GND (5 is a hidden stacked GND, 9 is GNDDetect), pin 2 to SWDIO (PA13), pin 4 to SWCLK (PA14), pin 10 to NRST; NC pins 6 (SWO) and 8 (TDI) if unused; pin 7 (KEY) is NC-typed already.
Mark every unused MCU pin as an explicit no-connect to reach ERC 0.
result: A reusable MCU skeleton: +3V3 star to all supplies/caps/VTref; GND absorbing all VSS (visible + hidden stacked), cap returns, and connector grounds; NRST/BOOT0/SWDIO/SWCLK signal nets; exhaustive NC markers elsewhere.
failure_modes: Hidden stacked pins (both VSS on MCUs and GND on the SWD connector) silently missing from power nets — the dominant ERC-failure class found while building the goldens.
On STM32G4 specifically, NRST shares pin with PG10 and BOOT0 shares with PB8 — those GPIOs are not free, and boot behavior also depends on option bits.
Floating BOOT0 = nondeterministic boot mode.
design_notes: Verified concretely on STM32G474RETx LQFP-64 across goldens 2-5; the recipe (100nF-per-VDD, VDDA cap, bulk cap, NRST cap, BOOT0 strap) generalizes across STM32 families with per-package pin lookup.
statement: Any STM32 design needs a canonical support skeleton before peripherals: all supply pins powered and decoupled, reset conditioned, boot mode strapped, and a debug port attached.

name: I2C sensor attach with pull-ups
problem: Connect an I2C peripheral to an MCU: the bus is open-drain and will not function without pull-ups, and sensors need local decoupling.
assumptions: Shared logic rail for MCU and sensor; standard-mode speeds; short traces
steps: Pick an I2C-capable MCU pin pair from the alternate-function table and resolve to physical package pins (e.g. STM32G474RETx LQFP-64: PB9/pin 62 = I2C1_SDA, PA15/pin 51 = I2C1_SCL, both AF4).
Create net 'SDA': MCU SDA pin + sensor SDA pin + pull-up resistor bottom; create net 'SCL': MCU SCL pin + sensor SCL pin + pull-up bottom.
One pull-up per line (10k standard mode; 2.2k-4.7k for fast mode or higher bus capacitance), tops on the logic rail. One pair per BUS, not per device.
Power the sensor from the rail with its own local 100nF.
NC any address/interrupt pins per the sensor's library pin types — pins already NC-typed in the symbol need no marker.
result: Multi-drop open-drain bus: SDA and SCL nets each shared by all bus members plus exactly one pull-up to the rail. Additional I2C devices join by adding their pins to the same two nets.
failure_modes: No pull-ups = dead bus (lines never rise). The repo's i2c_pullup lint detects this when nets are named SDA/SCL — keep that naming convention in generated designs.
Duplicated pull-ups from multiple modules can sum to too-strong pull (drivers can't sink to a valid low).
Mixed-rail buses: pull-ups to the wrong rail back-power or overstress the lower-voltage device.
design_notes: Generalized from golden 3 (STM32G474 + Si7050-A20, ERC 0); the pull-up-removal test proves the lint catches the canonical failure.
statement: Connect an I2C peripheral to an MCU: the bus is open-drain and will not function without pull-ups, and sensors need local decoupling.

name: SPI flash attach with CS/WP/HOLD handling
problem: Attach a SOIC-8 SPI NOR flash (W25Qxx-class) to an MCU so it is electrically sound in single-SPI mode and safe during MCU reset.
assumptions: 4-wire single SPI (quad mode unused); shared 3.3V rail
steps: Map MCU SPI signals to package pins (e.g. STM32G474 LQFP-64: PA5/19=SCK, PA6/20=MISO, PA7/21=MOSI, PA4/18=CS).
Point-to-point nets: MCU SCK -> flash CLK (pin 6); flash DO/IO1 (pin 2) -> MCU MISO; MCU MOSI -> flash DI/IO0 (pin 5).
Chip select: MCU GPIO + flash /CS (pin 1) + 10k pull-up to the rail, so the flash stays deselected while the MCU is in reset or bootloader.
Tie /WP (pin 3) and /HOLD (pin 7) each through their OWN 10k to the rail — never floating, and not a shared resistor, so they can become IO2/IO3 for quad mode later.
Flash VCC (pin 8) to rail with local 100nF; GND (pin 4) to ground.
result: Three point-to-point data/clock nets, one pulled-up chip-select net, two individually pulled-up active-low control nets, local decoupling. Directly extends to multiple SPI devices by sharing SCK/MISO/MOSI and adding one pulled-up CS per device.
failure_modes: Floating /HOLD pauses transfers randomly; low /WP blocks writes — the flash 'works in the lab, fails in the field' failure.
No CS pull-up: floating CS during reset lets noise clock spurious commands into the flash (worst case: corrupting it while a programmer runs).
DO/DI naming inversion vs MISO/MOSI (DO->MISO, DI->MOSI) — electrically silent, ERC-invisible, firmware-visible.
design_notes: Generalized from golden 4 (STM32G474 + W25Q32JVSS, ERC 0). Pull-ups instead of hard ties keep the quad-SPI upgrade path open.
statement: Attach a SOIC-8 SPI NOR flash (W25Qxx-class) to an MCU so it is electrically sound in single-SPI mode and safe during MCU reset.

name: UART debug header
problem: Expose an MCU UART on a pin header for logging/console/bootloader access via a USB-serial adapter.
assumptions: Logic-level UART (3.3V), not RS-232; adapter side does the TX/RX cross
steps: Map a USART to package pins (e.g. STM32G474 LQFP-64: PA9/43 = USART1_TX, PA10/44 = USART1_RX).
Use a 1x04 2.54mm header with pinout TX / RX / 3V3 / GND.
Net 'UART_TX': MCU TX pin -> header pin 1 (labeled from the BOARD's perspective).
Net 'UART_RX': header pin 2 -> MCU RX pin.
Header pin 3 to +3V3, pin 4 to GND.
result: Two point-to-point signal nets plus power and ground on a 4-pin header; the mating adapter connects its RX to the board's TX and vice versa.
failure_modes: Perspective confusion on TX/RX labels: label from the board's view and let the cable/adapter cross; labeling from the adapter's view yields a double cross and no comms.
Omitting GND on the header — UART has no return path and reads garbage.
5V-only adapters driving a 3.3V-only RX pin (check 5V tolerance before sharing the header with 5V adapters).
design_notes: Generalized from golden 5 (ERC 0). Including the 3V3 pin gives adapters a level reference and can power small targets; ordering TX/RX/3V3/GND keeps power pins adjacent at one end.
statement: Expose an MCU UART on a pin header for logging/console/bootloader access via a USB-serial adapter.

name: GPIO-driven status LED
problem: Add a firmware-controlled indicator LED to any MCU design with correct polarity and safe current.
assumptions: GPIO can source ~4-10 mA; generic LED with Vf ~2V
steps: Pick a free GPIO and resolve its package pin (e.g. PA5 = pin 19 on STM32G474 LQFP-64).
Net 'LED_CTRL': GPIO pin -> series resistor pin 1.
Net 'LED_A': resistor pin 2 -> LED anode (Device:LED pin 2).
LED cathode (Device:LED pin 1) to GND. Active-high: GPIO sources current.
Size R = (Vrail - Vf) / I: 330R gives ~4 mA at 3.3V or ~9 mA at 5V — visible and safe for MCU pins.
result: Series chain GPIO -> R -> LED(A->K) -> GND. Variant: for higher currents or shared-cathode constraints, flip to active-low (rail -> R -> LED -> GPIO sinks).
failure_modes: Polarity swap: in KiCad's Device:LED, pin 1 = cathode and pin 2 = anode — the number-order intuition ('pin 1 = anode') is wrong and the mistake passes ERC.
No series resistor: GPIO current-limits chaotically or the pin/LED degrades.
Exceeding per-pin or total-port current limits when driving several LEDs.
design_notes: Appears twice in the verified corpus: golden 1 (switch + R + LED at 5V) and golden 5 (GPIO + 330R + LED at 3.3V), both ERC 0 — same chain, different drive source.
statement: Add a firmware-controlled indicator LED to any MCU design with correct polarity and safe current.
